scores.evidence: BM25 matters here because support queries often contain exact terms like error codes, SKUs, and feature names.
scores.rationale: Hybrid RRF, rerank thresholds, and embedding-version handling are correct; minor issues like the sanitization claim and the cache/filter interplay are not deeply addressed.

scores.evidence: Resolve common support questions correctly using only official docs. When the bot can't, it hands off to a human smoothly.
scores.rationale: Covers core RAG support needs, with phased scope and an optional actions phase; account-specific scope is deferred rather than firmly decided.

scores.evidence: The orchestrator acts on the flags.
scores.rationale: Components and flows are consistent, but the visibility/entitlement filter and anonymous-versus-logged-in handling are only loosely tied together, and the query-rewrite filter extraction is not reconciled with authenticated filtering.

scores.evidence: Regression gate: run in CI on every change to prompts, models, chunking, or the index. Block deploys that regress past set thresholds.
scores.rationale: Golden set from real tickets, retrieval and answer metrics, judge calibration, red-team set, and post-launch review are present; thresholds are labeled initial but not justified, and the confidence threshold is only called calibrated.

scores.evidence: I don't know your docs platform, ticketing system, or traffic yet, so this plan assumes a typical setup
scores.rationale: States assumptions and open questions, with targets marked initial; it says little about which assumptions would change the design and how.

scores.evidence: Sensitive intents always go to a human. These include account security or compromise, billing disputes
scores.rationale: Covers hallucination, injection, stale docs, bot loops, LLM outage, and PII; it is thinner on partial ingestion failures, webhook misses, and cache poisoning.

scores.evidence: prompts, chunking settings, and model choices live in config with version IDs, so you can A/B test and roll back.
scores.rationale: Observability, versioning, and a fallback are covered, but there is no ownership or on-call, no alerting on specific signals, no index reindex or rollback procedure, and no incident handling.

scores.evidence: Use the small model for classification and rewriting. Cap context size.
scores.rationale: Controls are listed, but there is no per-conversation cost estimate, no scaling discussion, and no build-versus-buy reasoning; cost is asked about only as an open question.

scores.evidence: store the model version with each vector. Re-embed everything whenever the model changes.
scores.rationale: Embedding versioning and config-based rollback are recognized, but vendor options are left open with no isolation or exit discussion, and chunk ID and metadata schema commitments are not examined.

Query rewriting, reranking, an intent classifier, a verification pass and multiple guardrails are all in the MVP without measuring a simple baseline first, though they are mostly justified and not extreme.

scores.evidence: Audit docs (coverage, staleness, duplicates); pull the top 100 ticket intents; build the golden set; pick the stack
scores.rationale: The phased roadmap has durations, scope and team, with the golden set built early, but the stack is left undecided and there are no explicit go/no-go criteria between phases.

checklist.evidence: CMS webhooks trigger re-indexing of the changed article, plus a full nightly reconciliation that deletes unpublished articles. Target: changes are live within 15 minutes.
